cadence: weekly, Monday before the US open
method: Every Monday each open call is re-examined against the claims its note made. The numbers are computed from the record: where the call stands against what the note called for, how far the stop is, and a price-only range for where it can finish, drawn from the position's own recent volatility with no view assumed. The verdict is a judgment, stated with dated evidence: each claim the note relied on is re-measured and marked as holding or not, and the verdict has to follow from those marks. A broken thesis closes the call on the Scorecard from the review date. The return a note called for is written once and never changed.

latest.book_now: After this week's review the book holds five calls: short the S&P 500 against widening credit, long US energy stocks, long the yen, long US natural gas and short wheat through the fund. Four reasons are fully in place. Natural gas stays weakened: the oil-to-gas gap the note bought is now wider than when the call was made, but it widened the wrong way again, with gas down about 15% on the week on warm November forecasts while crude rose to $103, and the gas fund closed Friday about 6% under entry with the stop one more week like this away. Highest conviction is wheat, up about 14% on the short with nine sessions to run and funds still adding to shorts rather than buying back, followed by the new credit call, which is 1.7% in hand after three sessions with credit still widening, and energy stocks, up about 6% with oil at a three-year high. The yen call finally moved: dollar-yen fell about 1% to 156.49, a one-month low, with Tokyo still coordinating with the Bank of Japan ahead of its meeting this week. A reader holding the calls changes nothing today; the thing to watch is whether natural gas closes the week below 2.45, which would close that call at a loss, and whether the S&P 500 recovers toward 7,818, which would close the credit call.

book.basis: equal weight across the open calls, one unit each, trailing 63 sessions; a 21-session driftless range

book_risk.note: correlations are of daily mark changes over the trailing 63 sessions; exposure is the position's % move per 1% in equities or the dollar and per +10bp in the 10-year yield

calls.title: Oil carries a war premium. US natural gas carries none.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median front-month gas gain over three months after an oil-to-gas ratio reading at or above the 95th percentile (42 episodes since 2004)
calls.expected_basis: the fund's loss to Friday's close (about -5.8%) plus the base-rate catch-up scaled to the seven weeks left (about +4.2% of the +7.6% three-month median, since the ratio is again above the 95th percentile), less about half a point for the fund's cost of rolling contracts
calls.view_now: The gap between oil and gas is now wider than when the call was made, which is the setup the note bought, but for a second week it widened instead of closing, and this time gas did the damage, falling about 15% on warm November forecasts even though storage grew less than usual. The gas fund closed Friday about 6% under entry and gas traded near 2.52 on Monday morning, about 3% above the weekly-close stop at 2.45. Funds are still adding to a record short, which is fuel for a reversal if the weather turns, but with seven weeks left we now expect the call to finish a little under water rather than to earn what the note called for.
calls.action_reason: The reason for the call is more extreme than at publication and the record short in gas has not started to unwind, so from here the expected finish is better than cutting at Friday's loss. The stop does the work now: a weekly close below 2.45 closes the call, and that could happen this week. The review will close it if the ratio swings back toward oil-cheap or funds start buying their gas short back while gas keeps falling.
calls.weakened_reason: Every condition still holds, but the week went hard against the way the note said the gap would close: gas fell about 15% to 2.64 on forecasts of above-normal temperatures across the Midwest and East into early November, while crude rose to $103, so the oil-to-gas gap widened from both ends to a wider extreme than at publication. The gas fund closed Friday at 9.58, about 6% under entry, and the stop is within one more week like this.

calls.title: The last buyers just showed up in wheat
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate between its one-month (−5.3%) and three-month (−6.6%) medians for a two-month horizon, taken as a short return
calls.expected_basis: the gain to Friday's close (about +13.8% on the short) less a little give-back over the nine sessions left, with no further drift added because the fund selling the note relied on is done
calls.view_now: Wheat fell again, from 660.5 to 625, and the fund the reader shorts closed Friday at 22.83, about 14% below entry. Funds have not only finished selling their record length but are now building a short, so the buying that would end the move has not begun. With nine sessions left and the target passed weeks ago, we expect the call to finish close to where it is, well above what the note called for.
calls.action_reason: Driver intact, target passed and the stop far away. It runs to its early-November horizon, where the scorer settles it; the review will close it early only if funds start buying wheat back.

calls.title: The record yen rescue looks dead. So did the last three at exactly this point.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's target: 147 on dollar-yen by late January 2027, the median months-two-to-six move applied from 157.34, roughly +6% on the fund
calls.expected_basis: the note's months-two-to-six median move applied from Friday's 156.49 (about +6.5% on dollar-yen to 147), plus the small gain so far (about +0.4% on the fund), cut by about one and a half points because the record rests on three episodes; raised from last week's 4.5 because the move has now started with thirteen weeks left
calls.view_now: The move the note waited for began this week: dollar-yen fell about 1% to 156.49, a one-month low, as a hotter Japanese inflation report added to the case for another Bank of Japan rate rise and falling US yields narrowed the gap between the two. Tokyo is still coordinating with the central bank ahead of its meeting this week and has not stepped back. The fund is only slightly above entry, so most of the gain is still to come; we now expect somewhat more than last week, though still a little less than the note called for because only three prior episodes stand behind it.
calls.action_reason: The driver is in place, the authorities are still engaged, the move has begun and the stop is well away. The review will weaken the call if the Bank of Japan signals no further rises this week or dollar-yen pushes back toward 162 without a response.

calls.title: Yields and oil are surging together. Energy stocks gained after that in 7 of 8 cases.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return: the average fund return over six months in the eight earlier cases, with the 10% weekly-close exit applied
calls.expected_basis: the note's base rate held, because every condition holds; the gain so far (about +6.3% at Friday's close) is part of that path, and the two narrower oil-above-$90 cases (+8.7% and +4.6%) argue against adding to it
calls.view_now: Oil pushed to a three-year high of $103 on Friday and the energy fund closed at 69.33, about 6% above entry, while the broad market fell. Bond yields eased again, from 5.09% to 5.00%, and are now the closest of the three conditions to failing, though still a quarter-point clear. With the setup stronger on oil and the fund ahead of the path, we still expect the call to pan out roughly as the note said; the two earlier cases with oil above $90 made less than the average, so we do not raise the number.
calls.action_reason: Every condition holds and the exit is about 15% below the market. The watch is bond yields: a slide below 4.75% would weaken the call, and they moved a quarter-point closer this week.

calls.title: Credit spreads widening, S&P 500 likely to close the gap
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return: the median S&P 500 fall over fifteen sessions in the five earlier cases (3.2%), as a short of the index, which is what the Scorecard marks
calls.expected_basis: the note's base rate, unchanged, because both conditions hold and the first three sessions (index down 1.7%) sit inside the path of the five cases, whose largest rise inside any window was 1.2%; the easing in the 10-year yield removes the one regime mismatch the note sized down for, but five cases are too few to raise the number
calls.view_now: Credit kept widening after the note went up: the high-yield spread reached 340 basis points on Thursday, from 333 at publication, and the S&P 500 fell from 7,757 to 7,624 by Friday, 1.7% in three sessions, which is on the path of the five earlier cases. The 10-year yield, the one thing in the record that did not match today's setup, eased from 5.13% to 5.00% this week, which takes some of that worry away. With thirteen sessions left and the stop 2.5% away, we still expect the call to finish about where the note said, around 3% lower on the index.
calls.action_reason: Both conditions hold and the move is under way. The call runs to its mid-November horizon; the scorer closes it on a close above 7,818, and the review will weaken it if the high-yield spread falls back below 300 basis points.
